message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC).

**Key figures from the 10-K (FY2024):**
- **Total net sales: $391,035 million (~$391.0B)**, up 2% from $383,285M in FY2023
- Product sales $294,866M; Services $96,169M (+13% y/y)
- Gross margin $180,683M (46.2% of net sales, up from 44.1%)
- Operating income $123,216M (up from $114,301M)
- Net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08 — depressed by a one-time $10.2B net income-tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision; operating income still grew ~7.8%
- Operating cash flow $118,254M; cash + marketable securities $140.8B

**Rationale:** Revenue returned to growth (+2%), driven by record Services growth (+13%) and margin expansion (gross margin 46.2% vs 44.1%), while operating income rose nearly 8% on flat-ish revenue — the net income decline was non-operational (a one-time Irish tax charge) and doesn't reflect deterioration in the underlying business. Strong cash generation and a $110B buyback authorization support the equity. That justifies a modest, mandate-compliant addition.

**What I did:** Placed one buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at $222.95** (~0.1% above the ask of $222.72, well within "close to current market"), total ~$9,810 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap. The order filled at $222.95 for a total of ~$9,809.80; cash remains in the account (no withdrawals), and AAPL is one of the two permitted tickers.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.95, 44 shares = $9,809.80 spent (limit was slightly above ask of 222.72, so fill was at limit — a bit unfortunate but within "close to market").

Summary.
